what: T1.B -- LISTWISE / learning-to-rank vs POINTWISE on IDENTICAL features, folds, architecture and model-selection criterion. Tests whether the incumbent's pointwise-then-argmax objective mismatch explains the best-of-8 selector gap.
endpoint: selection efficiency P(pick correct | correct present) at N=8, pooled and per dataset, paired bootstrap 95% CI, nboot=10000, seed=0
incumbent: ckpts/train/lora_verifier_disjoint (clean L1 image-disjoint LoRA verifier), sel_eff 0.775204

protocol.folds: 5-fold GroupKFold, groups = md5 of decoded RGB pixels of the eval image (image-disjointness asserted in code)
protocol.auroc_caveat: pooled candidate AUROC for fitted arms is computed on out-of-fold scores that were standardised per fold, so it is approximate; sel_eff/sel_acc are exact (argmax is within-question and invariant to any per-fold affine rescale).
protocol.epoch_selection: inner 4-fold GroupKFold on the training folds; the epoch maximising INNER VALIDATION SELECTION EFFICIENCY is chosen -- identical criterion for every arm
protocol.ensembling: 5 inits per fold, averaged in globally z-scored raw-score space, identical for every arm
protocol.degenerate_lists: listwise/pairwise objectives (and the pointwise_bce_nondeg control) are trained only on lists that contain at least one correct and one wrong candidate; plain pointwise_bce sees every list.
protocol.architecture: 2x64 ReLU MLP scoring each candidate independently (and a linear variant); the loss is the ONLY thing that differs between arms
protocol.honesty: arms whose feature set is V or FULL use the incumbent verifier's score, which exists only on the 2345 EVAL items (the adapter was never run over the 16,621 disjoint train items). They are cross-fitted DIAGNOSTICS / upper bounds, not deployable numbers. The NOV arms use no incumbent-derived feature and carry no such caveat.

D1_sel_eff_decomposition.note: Only the mixed stratum is winnable, so a +0.021 pooled sel_eff win (the 2-sigma detection floor) requires flipping 31 of the 852 mixed items net, i.e. +0.036 on the mixed stratum.

D2_label_noise_identical_strings_differe.why_it_matters: On these questions two candidates are the SAME STRING with different judge labels, so no function of (image, question, answer) -- pointwise, listwise or pairwise -- can order them. On the affected mixed items the expected efficiency of any such scorer is bounded below 1 by construction.

D3_rank_of_best_correct_when_incumbent_e.reading: A ranking loss can only help by promoting a correct candidate past the incumbent's top-1. If the mass sits at rank 2 the errors are near-ties a ranking objective could plausibly repair; if it is spread toward rank 8 the incumbent is not mis-ordering, it is unable to see the correct answer at all.

D4_monotone_invariance.statement: Selection is argmax WITHIN a question, so sel_eff is exactly invariant to any strictly increasing global transform of the score. Any objective change that only recalibrates -- which is most of what a pointwise->listwise swap does to a score already fit on the same features -- moves selection by exactly 0. To move sel_eff an objective must change the WITHIN-QUESTION ORDER on a mixed-label list.
D4_monotone_invariance.empirical_check_V_only_arms: the mlp_V_* arms in the main artifact: all four objectives on the single incumbent-score feature give delta 0.0000 with a degenerate CI, confirming the pipeline adds nothing when the features cannot express a reordering.

D5_in_sample_leaky_ceiling.protocol: a 2x256 MLP fit on the EVAL labels themselves and scored in-sample -- deliberately leaky. It upper-bounds what these features can express at unlimited capacity, with generalisation removed as a factor.

verdict.headline: NEGATIVE, cleanly diagnosed. The pointwise/argmax objective mismatch is NOT what limits best-of-8 selection here. Across 15 objective contrasts holding features, folds, architecture, optimiser, epoch-selection criterion and ensembling fixed, no listwise or pairwise objective beat its pointwise twin: best point estimate +0.0082 sel_eff (CI [-0.0054,+0.0225], spans 0), five contrasts significantly NEGATIVE, largest -0.1117.
verdict.detection_floor_from_the_test_plan: a win must be >= +0.021 sel_eff to clear 2 sigma; nothing here approaches it
verdict.the_objective_is_not_the_variable_that_m: Compare the two contrasts that isolate it. (a) pointwise_bce_nondeg vs pointwise_bce -- same objective, training restricted to the 852 non-degenerate lists -- moves selection by -0.0020 [-0.0116,+0.0075] (MLP/NOV). (b) listnet vs pointwise_bce_nondeg -- SAME restricted training set, only the loss differs -- moves it -0.0817 [-0.1042,-0.0586]. So the loss swap is doing the damage, and its sign is negative.
verdict.mechanism_why_listwise_loses: It is not that the listwise objective optimises the wrong thing -- it optimises the right thing better. With label leakage and unlimited capacity (diagnostics D5) the listwise arms reach a HIGHER in-sample selection efficiency than pointwise on identical features (NOV: 0.956 listnet / 0.971 anypos vs 0.918 pointwise). Out of fold that reverses (0.645 / 0.657 vs 0.729). The listwise objective is the higher-variance estimator: it sees only within-question contrasts, and 1493 of 2345 lists (63.7%) are all-correct or all-wrong and therefore carry zero gradient for it, so it trains on 36.3% of the data while pointwise BCE uses all 18,760 candidate labels. It overfits the contrast it is asked to model.
verdict.why_the_ceiling_is_not_a_mis_ordering: On the 330 mixed-list questions the incumbent gets wrong, the best correct candidate sits at rank 2 only 22.1% of the time; the rank histogram is nearly flat out to rank 8 (mean rank 4.46) and the median score gap to it is 0.132. A ranking objective repairs near-ties. These are not near-ties -- the incumbent is not mis-ordering candidates it can see, it cannot see the correct one. Judge label noise is ruled out as an explanation: ZERO of 2345 questions contain the same candidate string with two different judge labels (0 inconsistent pairs out of 30,326 duplicate pairs).
verdict.reproduces_N25_at_a_new_level: N25 found within-question Bradley-Terry on the LoRA's Yes/No logit gave per-answer AUROC +0.030 and selection +0.000. The same dissociation reappears here at the feature level and in BOTH directions: mlp_FULL_pointwise_bce lifts candidate AUROC 0.8856 -> 0.9005 and moves sel_eff by exactly +0.0000, while mlp_FULL_listnet drops AUROC to 0.5345 (listwise scores carry no global calibration) and moves sel_eff by only -0.0054. Ranking quality and selection are close to decoupled on this data.
verdict.what_this_closes: Together with N25 this settles the objective question for this selector: the constraint is INFORMATIONAL, not objective-level. Loss-function work on the existing score function is a dead branch at both the LoRA level (N25) and the feature level (here). Only candidates that inject NEW information remain live.
honest_caveats: Every V/FULL arm uses the incumbent verifier score as a feature, and that score exists only on the 2345 eval items (the adapter was never run over the 16,621 disjoint train items). Those arms are cross-fitted DIAGNOSTICS, not deployable numbers. The NOV arms carry no such caveat and are uniformly worse.
The comparison BETWEEN arms is internally valid regardless: identical folds, identical features, identical leakage exposure, identical model-selection criterion.

Folds are image-disjoint (md5 of decoded RGB pixels, asserted in code); the paired bootstrap is reported both question-level and image-clustered, and the two agree to 4 decimal places on the best arm.

This tests learning-to-rank OBJECTIVES over a fixed feature/score function. It does not test set-aware ARCHITECTURES (T2.C Set-Encoder, T3.C pairwise distillation), where candidate i's score is a function of all 8 candidates. Nothing here speaks against those.

The listwise arms were given every fair advantage: the same epoch-selection criterion (inner-validation selection efficiency) all arms got, the same 5-init ensembling, and the standard LTR practice of dropping degenerate lists -- with pointwise_bce_nondeg as the control for that restriction.
